title: Entanglement-based Quantum Key Distribution With Classical Signals In Hollow-core Fiber
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 November 2026;
tldr: The paper demonstrates entanglement-based quantum key distribution coexisting with classical signals in hollow-core fiber.
motivation: Hollow-core fiber offers low nonlinearity and broad bandwidth, making it attractive for coexisting classical data and quantum signals in future quantum networks.
method: The authors implement entanglement-based QKD over hollow-core fiber while transmitting classical signals in the same fiber environment.
result: They show that entanglement-based QKD can operate alongside classical signals in hollow-core fiber, indicating feasibility for integrated quantum-classical networking.
conclusion: The work supports hollow-core fiber as a promising platform for entanglement distribution and QKD in network scenarios with classical traffic.

title: RF-free Control Of Nuclear Spins With Color Centers In Silicon Carbide
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 November 2026;
tldr: The paper demonstrates radio-frequency-free coherent control of nuclear spins in silicon carbide using color-center defect spins as local mediators.
motivation: Nuclear spins in SiC are attractive long-lived quantum memories and qubits, but conventional nuclear magnetic resonance control requires strong RF fields that are difficult to localize and integrate on chip, motivating all-electrical or defect-driven alternatives.
method: Color-center electronic spins in SiC are used to drive nuclear spin transitions via hyperfine and quadrupolar couplings, exploiting the defect spin as an on-chip actuator to achieve RF-free manipulation of nearby nuclear spins.
result: Coherent nuclear spin control is achieved without applied RF fields, enabling localized addressing of nuclear spins with the color center acting as a control knob.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable, RF-free route to nuclear spin manipulation in SiC, relevant for hybrid spin-register architectures and color-center-based quantum devices.

title: Compilation-informed Probabilistic Logical-error Cancellation
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 19 November 2026;
tldr: The paper introduces a compilation-informed probabilistic method for cancelling logical errors in quantum computations.
motivation: Logical errors remain a key obstacle to reliable quantum computation, and error-cancellation techniques may reduce their impact without full fault-tolerant overhead.
method: The authors combine quantum compilation with probabilistic logical-error cancellation, likely using compilation-derived noise information to tailor cancellation protocols.
result: The proposed approach is presented as a practical scheme for mitigating logical errors, with performance assessed in the context of compiled quantum circuits.
conclusion: Compilation-informed probabilistic logical-error cancellation offers a relevant route toward more reliable quantum information processing, though it is complementary to mainstream quantum error correction.

title: High-key-rate Fully-passive Quantum Access Network With Thermal Source
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 19 November 2026;
tldr: The paper demonstrates a high-key-rate fully-passive quantum access network using a thermal light source.
motivation: Quantum access networks are important for extending QKD to multiple users, and fully-passive architectures can reduce hardware complexity and active-device security risks while thermal sources offer practical advantages.
method: The authors propose and experimentally implement a fully-passive quantum access network based on a thermal source, targeting high secure key rates for multiple access users.
result: The scheme achieves high key rates in a fully-passive network configuration, indicating improved practicality for multi-user quantum access.
conclusion: Fully-passive QANs with thermal sources are a promising route toward scalable, low-cost, high-rate quantum-secure access networks.

title: Hardware-tailored Logical Clifford Circuits For Stabilizer Codes
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 12 November 2026;
tldr: The paper presents methods for constructing hardware-tailored logical Clifford circuits for stabilizer codes.
motivation: Logical gate implementation in stabilizer codes must respect hardware connectivity and noise constraints to be practical on near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors develop compiling/construction techniques that adapt logical Clifford operations to the underlying hardware architecture while preserving stabilizer-code structure.
result: The proposed approach yields hardware-aware logical Clifford circuits for stabilizer codes, likely improving implementability compared with hardware-agnostic constructions.
conclusion: Hardware-tailored logical Clifford synthesis is useful for making stabilizer-code computation more practical, though it is an incremental contribution relative to core quantum information theory interests.

title: Quantum Quickest Change Detection
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 November 2026;
tldr: The paper develops quantum quickest change detection, extending sequential change-point detection to quantum systems and measurements.
motivation: Classical quickest change detection is well established, but quantum settings require new statistical and measurement-theoretic tools for detecting abrupt changes in quantum states or channels as quickly as possible.
method: It likely formulates the quantum change-point problem using quantum hypothesis testing and sequential decision rules, possibly deriving quantum CUSUM-type or Bayesian detection procedures and performance bounds.
result: The work presumably provides quantum detection algorithms and characterizes their delay/error tradeoffs relative to classical and optimal quantum benchmarks.
conclusion: Quantum quickest change detection offers a rigorous information-theoretic framework for sequential quantum monitoring, with potential applications in quantum sensing, communication, and fault detection.

title: CryoCMOS Rf Multiplexer For Superconducting Qubit Control, Readout And Flux Biasing At Millikelvin Temperatures With Picowatt Power Consumption
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 14 November 2026;
tldr: The paper presents a cryo-CMOS RF multiplexer for controlling, reading out, and flux-biasing superconducting qubits at millikelvin temperatures with picowatt power consumption.
motivation: Scaling superconducting qubit systems requires reducing the wiring and heat load associated with room-temperature control and readout electronics, motivating low-power cryogenic multiplexing at the millikelvin stage.
method: The authors design and characterize a cryogenic CMOS RF multiplexer operating at millikelvin temperatures, intended for qubit control, readout, and flux biasing with extremely low power dissipation.
result: The multiplexer enables RF signal routing for superconducting qubit operations while consuming only picowatts of power, supporting more scalable cryogenic control architectures.
conclusion: This is a relevant hardware engineering advance for superconducting qubit platforms, but its contribution is primarily cryo-CMOS control electronics rather than a quantum-information, thermodynamic, or network-protocol result.

title: Element-specific, Non-destructive Profiling Of Two-dimensional Dopant Layers In Silicon
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 November 2026;
tldr: The paper presents an element-specific, non-destructive method for profiling two-dimensional dopant layers in silicon.
motivation: Precise characterization of shallow dopant profiles is important for silicon-based quantum devices and nanoscale electronics, but existing profiling methods can be destructive or lack elemental specificity.
method: The authors use synchrotron-based X-ray techniques to probe dopant layers in silicon without removing material, enabling element-specific depth profiling.
result: They obtain non-destructive, element-specific profiles of two-dimensional dopant layers, resolving their spatial distribution in silicon.
conclusion: The work provides a characterization tool relevant to dopant-based silicon architectures, but it does not directly address quantum information processing or hybrid quantum system performance.
